claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have a son Alex who is 17 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17, I need to check if he meets the requirements for children aged 16 or over. According to the rules, you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, studying for A-levels, doing a traineeship, or in another form of approved education or training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any approved education at the moment. But he has started an apprenticeship - he's doing one in Wales.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is important - the rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England. However, Alex is doing an apprenticeship in Wales, not England.

Before I make a final assessment, I need to ask a few more questions to ensure I have all the relevant information:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and/or pay for his upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I'm responsible for him - I pay for everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one final question:

**Has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else planning to claim for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him or planning to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. 

Based on what you've told me, I need to let you know that I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's the situation:**

The rules I have access to specifically state that Child Benefit stops if your child starts an **apprenticeship in England**. However, Alex has started an apprenticeship in **Wales**, not England.

The rules don't clearly address whether apprenticeships in Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland are treated the same way as apprenticeships in England for Child Benefit purposes. Because of this gap in the guidance, I cannot definitively say whether you are eligible or ineligible.

**What you should do:**

I strongly recommend that you **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to clarify how Alex's Welsh apprenticeship affects your Child Benefit entitlement. They will be able to give you a definitive answer based on their complete understanding of how apprenticeships in different parts of the UK are treated.

You can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office by phone or post - they'll be able to help you with this specific situation.
